brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether wearing mineral-infused clothing helps muscles recover after a hard bout of unaccustomed exercise in healthy adults aged 18 to 45 who have not done lower-body resistance or jump training in the last 6 months.

The main question it aims to answer is: does wearing the mineral-infused garment lead to greater recovery of leg muscle strength (maximal voluntary isometric contraction of the knee extensors) 72 hours after exercise, compared with wearing an identical garment without the mineral infusion?

Researchers will also compare the two garments for recovery of jump performance, muscle soreness and blood creatine kinase (a marker of muscle damage), and will describe garment comfort and tolerability.

Participants will:

* Complete electronic consent, an online screening questionnaire and a video screening call
* Attend the study site on four consecutive days
* On Day 1, complete baseline tests, then perform 100 drop jumps (5 sets of 20) to cause muscle soreness
* Wear their allocated garment for at least 16 hours a day (day and overnight) for the following 72 hours and keep a daily wear log
* Have strength, jump and soreness tests and a finger-prick blood sample at each visit (24, 48 and 72 hours after exercise)
primary_outcomes: Change in maximal voluntary isometric contraction (MVC) force of the knee extensors at 72 hours post-exercise
title: Mineral-Infused Clothing for Recovery From Muscle Soreness and Muscle Damage After Exercise

brief_summary:
Females with Fabry disease are characterized by variable phenotypes regarding time of onset, severity of symptoms and progression of disease due to the random inactivation of X chromosome leading to a cellular mosaic of mutated and wild genotypes.

Left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH) is a relatively late manifestation, appearing typically after the third decade in men and the fourth decade in women. Cardiac involvement progresses throughout life in Fabry females and is the first cause of death but in contrast to males, the loss of myocardial function and the development of fibrosis do not necessarily require myocardial hypertrophy in female with FD.

The presence of overt LVH and myocardial fibrosis has been shown to negatively affect treatment outcome, suggesting the importance of early initiation of treatment.

Multiparametric cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) is able to detect sphingolipid infiltration by identifying a pre-LVH phase of cardiac FD defined by a low myocardial native T1, occurring in up to 60% of FD patients, with a concomitant slight elevated LV ejection fraction and electrocardiographic (ECG) changes. Low myocardial T1 values are independently associated with FD progression and are risk factors for clinical worsening.

Normal native T1 value is known to be higher in healthy young women than in men but prevalence of low native T1 in Fabry females has not been correctly assessed so far.

Treating Fabry females at the appropriate time is still a major issue and remains questionable as therapeutic and financial burden has to be balanced with severity status.

However, low native myocardial T1 in CMR is an early marker of cardiac impairment in FD that could justify adapting the therapeutic initiation notably in women. This is of paramount importance as early treatment may provide more benefit before occurrence of irreversible lesions such as LVH and fibrosis.
primary_outcomes: Proportion of non-treated non-hypertrophic Fabry females for whom the indication for specific Fabry therapy (ERT or chaperone) is modified (i.e. established) based on additional information provided by low native myocardial T1 value.
title: Therapeutic Implications of CMR Low Native T1 in Non-treated Non-hypertrophic Females With Fabry Disease (FD)

brief_summary:
Male factors account for approximately 50% of infertility cases. The principal etiologies of male infertility include sexual dysfunction, semen abnormalities arising from various etiologies, and idiopathic infertility. Semen analysis remains a key method for assessing male fertility, with semen abnormalities representing the most significant contributing factors. Common semen abnormalities include oligozoospermia, asthenozoospermia, and teratozoospermia. In recent years, elevated sperm DNA fragmentation (SDF) has emerged as an important and increasingly prevalent cause of male infertility. The World Health Organization (WHO) Laboratory Manual for the Examination and Processing of Human Semen, Sixth Edition, likewise emphasizes the importance of sperm DNA integrity, presents several techniques, and outlines the role of SDF testing in male infertility In infertile couples, the male sperm DFI is significantly higher than that of men with normal fertility (24.5% vs 17%), and the proportion of DFI \> 30% among men in infertile couples is greater. DFI is significantly associated with recurrent pregnancy loss. A meta-analysis shows that SDF is associated with sporadic miscarriage. Recent animal studies indicate that SDF may lead to fragmentation and random distribution of paternal chromosomal segments in the developing embryo, resulting in mosaicism of different genotypes within cells. Collectively, these findings suggest that increased SDF may elevate the risk of embryonic abnormalities. In IUI cycles, low SDF is associated with higher clinical pregnancy and live birth rates. IVF-ET studies indicate a significant association between high SDF and poorer embryo quality. The clinical pregnancy rate in the higher sperm DFI group is significantly lower than that in the low-DFI group.

Follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) plays a well-established role in human spermatogenesis. In most cases of azoospermia due to hypogonadotropic hypogonadism (HH), spermatogenesis can be effectively initiated. For patients with oligoasthenoteratospermia (OAT) who have low FSH levels, FSH may be administered at the same dose used for HH, enabling these infertile men to benefit from gonadotropin-based therapy. However, in some countries, FSH is not approved for male infertility treatment. Several clinical trials have evaluated recombinant FSH therapy in men with primary infertility, showing significant improvements in sperm concentration but little or no effect on progressive motility. However, most previous studies focused on men with oligoasthenoteratozoospermia or hypogonadotropic hypogonadism. It remains unclear whether HMG therapy benefits infertile men with isolated DFI elevation but normal conventional sperm count and normal sex hormone levels. This patient subgroup represents a clinical dilemma, as treatment options are limited. Therefore, we conducted this trial to evaluate the efficacy of HMG in improving DFI in this specific population.

This study aims to evaluate the efficacy of HMG treatment on sperm DFI and conventional parameters, sex hormone levels, and seminal plasma biochemical markers in infertile men with abnormal sperm DFI through a prospective controlled design.
primary_outcomes: sperm DFI
title: HMG Treatment Reduces Sperm DNA Fragmentation

brief_summary:
Chronic fatiguing illnesses such as Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome (ME/CFS), Fibromyalgia, and Long COVID are becoming a major global health challenge. They cause severe personal and social strain and have no proven, widely effective treatments. Although these conditions have different names, they share many symptoms: long-lasting fatigue that doesn't improve with rest, worsening of symptoms after activity (post-exertional malaise), difficulties with thinking ("brain fog"), poor sleep, and widespread pain. Increasing evidence shows that these illnesses also share similar underlying biological problems. These include ongoing inflammation, problems with the autonomic nervous system (which controls automatic body functions), poor function of the blood vessels, and reduced energy production in cells.

Whole-Body Cryotherapy (WBCT) is emerging as a promising non-drug treatment that may help break these cycles. WBCT involves very short, controlled exposure to extreme cold (around -110°C to -160°C). This triggers a rapid response across the nervous, immune, and metabolic systems. The cold acts as a powerful stimulus, encouraging the body to reset imbalanced systems. A session briefly narrows blood vessels and then causes them to widen again, improving blood flow and supporting healthy vessel function. WBCT also appears to reduce inflammation, lower oxidative stress, and improve parasympathetic ("rest-and-recover") nervous system activity.

Early studies in ME/CFS and related conditions are encouraging. Small trials have reported reduced fatigue, clearer thinking, and better autonomic regulation after a course of WBCT sessions, with good safety. Research has also shown changes in blood-brain barrier proteins after WBCT, suggesting it may help repair "leaky" barriers that can drive symptoms in ME/CFS and Long COVID.

By acting on inflammation, blood flow, and nervous system balance at the same time, WBCT could offers a scientifically grounded and potentially transformative approach in understanding the mechanism behind observed treatment effect.
primary_outcomes: Feasibility outcome measurements
title: Whole-body Cryotherapy in Those With Chronic Fatigue: A Feasibility Study

brief_summary:
Bladder cancer is one of the most common malignancies worldwide and represents a major global health burden. According to the GLOBOCAN 2022 estimates, approximately 614,298 new cases and 220,596 deaths from bladder cancer were reported worldwide, making it the ninth most commonly diagnosed malignancy globally.

Non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC), comprising Ta, T1, and carcinoma in situ (CIS), accounts for approximately three-quarters of newly diagnosed bladder cancers. Although NMIBC is confined to the mucosa or submucosa, it represents a heterogeneous group of tumors with markedly different risks of recurrence and progression, with the highest risk observed in high-grade and high-risk disease.

NMIBC is classified according to the risk of recurrence and progression into low-, intermediate-, high-, and very-high-risk groups. Risk stratification incorporates tumor stage, histological grade, tumor size, number of tumors, recurrence pattern, presence of CIS, age, and other adverse pathological and clinical features. High-grade histology, particularly T1 high-grade disease, is associated with a substantially increased risk of progression to muscle-invasive bladder cancer.

Risk Stratification of Non-Muscle-Invasive Bladder Cancer Risk group Main clinical and pathological characteristics Low-risk Primary, solitary, small low-grade Ta tumor without CIS and without significant adverse risk factors Intermediate-risk Tumors that do not fulfill the criteria for low-, high-, or very-high-risk disease High-risk Includes high-grade T1 tumors and CIS, as well as selected high-grade Ta/T1 tumors with additional adverse risk factors Very-high-risk High-grade tumors with multiple adverse features, including selected T1 high-grade tumors associated with CIS and/or multiple additional risk factors Risk classification should follow current guideline-defined criteria and should not be based on histological grade alone.

The management of high-risk NMIBC is based on complete transurethral resection of the bladder tumor (TURBT), followed by risk-adapted intravesical therapy. Full-dose intravesical Bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG) with maintenance therapy for one to three years remains an established standard treatment for high-risk disease, while radical cystectomy should be discussed in selected patients, particularly those with very-high-risk features.

T1 high-grade disease represents a particularly challenging subgroup because of its substantial potential for recurrence and progression despite bladder-preserving treatment. Clinical series of patients treated with TURBT followed by BCG have demonstrated considerable rates of both recurrent and progressive disease, emphasizing the need for effective treatment strategies in patients at high risk of treatment failure.

Radiotherapy has historically had a limited role in NMIBC. Nevertheless, its biological activity against urothelial carcinoma and its established role in bladder-preserving treatment of selected muscle-invasive bladder cancer have provided a rationale for investigating radiotherapy at earlier stages of bladder cancer. Modern radiotherapy techniques may allow treatment of the bladder while limiting radiation exposure to surrounding normal tissues.

Clinical evidence for radiotherapy in high-risk NMIBC has been reported since the early 1980s. Retrospective series evaluating radiotherapy in high-risk T1 bladder cancer demonstrated clinically meaningful complete response rates, local control, long-term survival, and bladder preservation. These findings suggest that radiotherapy may represent a potential bladder-preserving treatment option in carefully selected patients.

A systematic review and meta-analysis evaluating radiotherapy for high-risk NMIBC identified 13 studies involving 746 patients. The reported five-year recurrence-free survival, cancer-specific survival, and overall survival were 54%, 86%, and 72%, respectively. Approximately 13% of patients subsequently underwent salvage radical cystectomy and 9% developed metastatic disease. However, the available evidence was considered low quality because most studies were retrospective and heterogeneous, emphasizing the need for prospective clinical evaluation.

The potential role of radiotherapy in BCG-naïve high-risk NMIBC is of clinical interest because it could provide a bladder-preserving local treatment approach without prolonged intravesical therapy in selected patients. However, current guidelines do not consider radiotherapy a standard replacement for BCG-naïve high-risk NMIBC, and prospective evidence remains limited.

Therefore, there is a need for prospective evaluation of radiotherapy as a bladder-preserving treatment strategy in selected patients with high-risk NMIBC, who present without previous BCG exposure, and Evaluation of local disease control, bladder preservation, progression, survival, and treatment-related toxicity may help clarify the potential role of RTH
primary_outcomes: Complete Response (CR) Rate
title: The Role of Definitive Radiotherapy in Non Muscle Invasive Bladder Cancer

brief_summary: This prospective, single-center, observational pilot study evaluated an investigational wearable tissue oximeter (NIRSense Argus Oximetry System, also called Envello Core) in adult outpatients with chronic heart failure in New York Heart Association (NYHA) class I, II, or III at Jackson Heart Clinic in Jackson, Mississippi. During one routine clinic visit, participants wore three adhesive optical sensors, on the forearm, the thigh, and the sternum, while completing three standard tests: a blood pressure cuff occlusion of the arm (vascular occlusion test), a six-minute walk test, and a change from lying down to standing. The sensors use near-infrared spectroscopy to record changes in tissue oxygenation. The study compared tissue oxygenation responses across NYHA classes and with standard clinical measures (blood pressure, pulse rate, pulse oximetry, and walk distance). Participation added about 30 minutes to the visit, with no follow-up. Fifty participants were enrolled. No treatment decisions were based on the study device.

brief_summary: This study evaluates two different control strategies for a rehabilitation device that combines recumbent leg-cycling with functional electrical stimulation (FES) of the quadriceps muscle. The device assists pedaling using a motor and electrical stimulation, and is intended for use after knee surgery (such as ACL reconstruction) or in other lower-limb rehabilitation. During muscle stimulation, fatigue can develop, which reduces the force produced by the stimulated muscle. This study compares a standard control strategy with a new strategy that adjusts stimulation based on the muscle's fatigue level, measured in real time. Healthy adult volunteers will complete two sessions on a recumbent stationary bicycle, 2 to 7 days apart. Each session lasts about 60 minutes and includes periods of pedaling with electrical stimulation, as well as isometric wall squats to induce muscle fatigue. Muscle activity, pedal force, and pedal position will be recorded throughout. The goal is to determine which control strategy produces more mechanical work from the leg muscles and better tracks the desired pedaling pattern, especially as fatigue develops.

primary_outcomes: Mechanical work performed during FES-assisted pedaling

brief_summary: Title: Correlation Between Dynamic Postural Balance and Masticatory Efficiency in Edentulous Patients Rehabilitated with All-on-4 Fixed Prostheses Background: Total tooth loss (edentulism) alters sensory feedback from the mouth, which can negatively affect head orientation, body alignment, and overall balance, increasing the risk of falls in older adults. While complete dentures replace missing teeth, their lack of stability often limits full recovery of chewing function and balance. Fixed All-on-4 implant restorations provide a rigid, bone-anchored base that restores full functional efficiency and stabilizes the occlusion. Objective: The purpose of this study is to evaluate masticatory (chewing) efficiency in completely edentulous patients treated with maxillary and mandibular All-on-4 fixed implant-supported restorations, and to determine its correlation with dynamic postural body balance over time. Methods: Sixteen completely edentulous male patients aged 50-60 years received maxillary and mandibular All-on-4 fixed restorations with standardized lingualized occlusal schemes. Masticatory efficiency was assessed using a color-changing chewing gum (scored on a 1-5 scale). Dynamic postural body balance was measured using the Timed Up and Go (TUG) test, which records the time in seconds taken to stand from a chair, walk 3 meters, turn, walk back, and sit down. Measurements were recorded at three time points: immediately after final restoration delivery, at 3 months post-loading, and at 6 months post-loading. Expected Outcomes: The study aims to clarify how stabilizing the bite with fixed implant restorations impacts both chewing performance and dynamic walking balance, supporting neuromuscular adaptation and functional independence in edentulous patients.
primary_outcomes: Correlation Between Masticatory Efficiency and Dynamic Postural Balance(Spearman's rank correlation coefficient (rho))
title: Dynamic Postural Balance and Masticatory Efficiency in Edentulous Patients With All-on-4 Prostheses

brief_summary:
Peritoneal cancer is tricky to be managed. It is not easy to be detected or diagnosed at early stage without symptom, or with common symptoms of many diseases or discomfort and often leads to advance stage at time of diagnosis with few treatment options and limited life span. It is also challenging to handle peritoneal tumour as it usually involves large area in peritoneum, or spread widely throughout the surface of peritoneum if metastatic from other origins. Systemic therapy is the common way to treat peritoneal cacner if the disease is inoperable. However, the unsatisfied penetration rate significantly limits the anti-tumour effect of intraperitoneal chemotherapy even after various attempts and most approaches demonstrated limited efficiency. Effective treatment for peritoneal cancer is still scarce and necessary. While the tumour nature of peritoneal tumour consists of solid tumour and soft tissue tumour, depends on primary or secondary disease, Histotripsy, which can be used on most kinds of solid tumour as well as soft tissue tumour, may yield a new direction and insight on peritoneal cancer management.

Histotripsy is currently indicated for liver tumours, approved by FDA and has been investigated for many disease types in preclinical researches and carried out several clinical trials for liver tumour, benign prostatic hyperplasia, liver tumour combined with systemic therapy, renal tumour, pancreatic tumour, soft tissue tumours, abdominal tumour, calcific aortic valves, and pain in plantar fasciitis, with encouraging results in some clinical trials. As most clinical trials above are for solid tumour and soft tissue tumour that suit the tumour nature of peritoneal tumour, we believe that Histotripsy is also safe and feasible on human with peritoneal tumour. Considering nodal involvement also frequently comes with peritoneal cancer, we would like to conduct an investigation for Histotripsy in peritoneal tumour and lymph node.

Although the result of clinical trial in peritoneal tumour and lymph node are not available yet, HIFU (High Intensity Focused Ultrasound) as another non-invasive ablation also delivered by ultrasound wave which has been in clinical use for many years worldwide can be referenced for Histotripsy. The core difference of HIFU and Histotripsy is, HIFU employs thermal energy to induce coagulative necrosis, while Histotripsy utilises mechanical cavitation to disrupt tumour tissues and preserves adjacent critical structure without the issue of heat, which makes it safer than HIFU. According to some reviews of HIFU, it is obvious that HIFU is feasible and safe without significant adverse event for abdominal tumours including peritoneal tumour and lymph node. Consequently, Histotripsy as a non-thermal ablation and is considered to be safer than HIFU, should also be feasible and safe for peritoneal tumour and lymph node. Hence, it is time for Hong Kong to launch the investigation on the feasibility, safety, and efficacy of Histotripsy in peritoneal tumour and lymph node.
primary_outcomes: number of case proceed with Histotripsy
post procedure events
changes in tumour features
title: Histotripsy for Peritoneal Tumour and Lymph Node: a Pilot Study

brief_summary: PS52 is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, fully decentralized study sponsored by Bactolife A/S and conducted by People Science, Inc. It evaluates whether IgG Binding Protein LT (BP-LT), supports gut health in healthy US adults aged 18-70 travelling 7-21 days to Africa, Asia or Latin America/Caribbean countries. Participants are randomized 1:1 to BP-LT (one 75 mg capsule twice daily with food, 150 mg/day) or a matching placebo for the length of their trip. The primary endpoint is the change in GSRS total score from Baseline to End-of-Study versus placebo. Secondary endpoints cover stool frequency and consistency, gut microbiome and inflammation markers, appetite, cognitive function, safety, and outcomes in travellers who test positive for E. coli. Part 1 enrols 100-250 participants, and an interim analysis may expand the study to a maximum of 800 participants.
primary_outcomes: Change from Baseline to End-of-Study in Gastrointestinal Symptom Rating Scale (GSRS) total score in the IgG Binding Protein LT group versus the Placebo group.

brief_summary:
Parents of infants admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) face unique challenges in caring for their own health after giving birth. The demands of having a critically ill infant often make it difficult or impossible to attend postpartum care appointments, and research shows that NICU mothers are significantly more likely than other new mothers to develop postpartum depression and other health conditions, including hypertensive disorders of pregnancy. However, these conditions frequently go undetected and untreated because standard postpartum care systems are not designed to address the needs of NICU mothers, who often prioritize being present in the NICU over their own needs.

The PeliCaN (Postpartum Care in the NICU) Multi-Site trial will test whether trained postpartum doulas supporting mothers directly in the NICU can help close postpartum care gaps. Study doulas will provide emotional support, help mothers monitor their blood pressure, screen for postpartum depression, assist with scheduling and attending postpartum care visits, and connect families to community resources while their infant is in the NICU and after discharge for up to 6 months.

The study team will enroll approximately 756 mothers across 13 NICUs in the Metro-Philadelphia area. Participating NICUs will be randomly assigned to groups on a stepped-wedge schedule to begin offering the doula intervention. Mothers enrolled before their site begins the doula intervention will receive standard postpartum care and support; mothers enrolled after their site transitions to the intervention period will receive doula support. All participants will complete surveys at enrollment and at 6 months after birth and will have their medical records reviewed.

The study's main goals are to determine whether having a doula in the NICU helps mothers to receive recommended comprehensive postpartum care within the first 12 weeks after birth and will assess whether doula support reduces symptoms of postpartum depression and increases maternal transition to primary adult care by 6 months postpartum. The study will also examine the experience of implementing doulas in the NICU across multiple hospital sites among intervention participants and NICU staff members.
interventions: Postpartum Doula Support in the NICU
primary_outcomes: Receipt of Comprehensive Postpartum Care (Composite)
title: Postpartum Care in the NICU Multi-Site

brief_summary:
Preeclampsia is a multisystemic and multifactorial disorder that complicates pregnancy and is characterized by new-onset hypertension after the 20th week of gestation accompanied by proteinuria or systemic findings such as renal dysfunction, hepatic dysfunction, pulmonary edema, thrombocytopenia, or neurological symptoms including headache and visual disturbances. It represents a significant risk factor for maternal and fetal morbidity and mortality.

In normal pregnancy, trophoblasts invade and dilate the maternal spiral arteries, thereby increasing uteroplacental blood flow. In preeclampsia, however, inadequate trophoblastic invasion leads to defective placentation, resulting in uteroplacental hypoperfusion and ischemia. The hypoxic and ischemic placenta releases anti-angiogenic mediators into the maternal circulation, which disrupt maternal endothelial function. This endothelial dysfunction results in vasoconstriction, microthrombosis, and increased vascular permeability. Consequently, hypertension, renal and hepatic dysfunction, pulmonary edema, and neurological symptoms may develop in maternal organ systems.

The endothelial dysfunction observed in preeclampsia can also affect the microvascular structures of the eye, leading to circulatory disturbances at the level of the retina and choroid. Disruption of endothelial integrity, together with vasospasm and microthrombus formation, may cause reduced perfusion in the retinal and choroidal microcirculation, forming the basis of the ophthalmic manifestations of preeclampsia. Clinically, this condition may present with visual disturbances, blurred vision, scotomas, retinal edema, and choroidal thickening.

These microvascular changes can be evaluated noninvasively in outpatient settings using Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT) and Optical Coherence Tomography Angiography (OCTA). OCT and OCTA allow high-resolution imaging of retinal and choroidal structures and enable quantitative assessment of vascular parameters such as vessel density, the size of the foveal avascular zone (FAZ), and choriocapillaris flow voids. Through these techniques, microvascular hypoperfusion, loss of vascular integrity, and ischemic areas caused by endothelial damage associated with preeclampsia can be objectively identified.

The aim of this study is to evaluate ocular vascular changes associated with preeclampsia using OCT and OCTA
primary_outcomes: Retinal Vessel Density
Foveal Avascular Zone (FAZ) Area
title: Retinal and Choroidal Microcirculation in Preeclampsia: An OCTA Study

brief_summary:
This is a multicenter, observational, cross-sectional study designed to investigate whether a parsimonious set of low-cost, accessible functional, anthropometric, and physiological measurements can help identify multisystem clinical-physiological impairment in patients with Fontan circulation.

Fontan circulation is associated with long-term multisystem complications affecting cardiac, cardiopulmonary, hepatic, renal, nutritional-lymphatic, hematological, and metabolic function. Current surveillance may require multiple specialized, costly, and time-consuming investigations. This study will explore whether simple and easily repeatable measurements can provide an accessible complementary approach for the initial functional and clinical assessment of these patients.

Approximately 150 participants aged 14 to 60 years with Fontan circulation, recruited from 18 Spanish healthcare centers, will be included. Participants must have undergone Fontan surgery at least 2 years before inclusion and be clinically stable in outpatient follow-up.

Each participant will attend one study-specific visit lasting approximately 45-60 minutes. During this visit, functional, anthropometric, and physiological variables will be assessed. Functional measurements will include squat jump performance using the Samozino method and the five-times sit-to-stand test (5xSTS) using the Alcázar method. Anthropometric measurements will include body mass index, age- and sex-adjusted anthropometric indicators of muscularity, and calf and thigh circumferences. Physiological measurements will include resting heart rate and oxygen saturation, heart rate recovery after the 1-minute sit-to-stand test, and post-exercise oxygen saturation.

Clinical, laboratory, echocardiographic, and functional data obtained as part of routine clinical follow-up will also be collected. Whenever possible, routine clinical measurements will correspond to assessments performed on the same day as the functional evaluation; measurements obtained within a maximum window of ±15 days will also be considered.

The primary analysis will evaluate the association between the candidate low-cost measurements and the presence of clinical-physiological impairment affecting two or more organ or functional domains. Additional analyses will investigate their ability to identify patients with impairment in at least one domain and to discriminate increasing levels of multisystem clinical-physiological burden.

The study will not involve any therapeutic intervention or prospective study-specific follow-up. The results will be interpreted as cross-sectional associations and will not establish causal or longitudinal prognostic relationships.
primary_outcomes: Multisystem clinical-physiological impairment affecting ≥2 domains
title: A Simple Method for Monitoring the End-organ Function in Patients With Fontan Circulation.

brief_summary:
This randomized, placebo-controlled clinical trial aims to investigate the effects of oral cholera vaccine administration on three aspects of gut health in healthy adult community members aged 18 years and older: (1) the composition and function of gut microbiota, (2) serum inflammatory cytokine levels, and (3) bowel habits. The study is designed as an exploratory/basic science investigation to generate hypotheses about how cholera vaccination may influence intestinal health in healthy populations. The findings from this study may provide valuable insights into vaccine-induced changes in the gut microbiome and immune responses, which could inform future research on oral vaccines and their extra-intestinal effects.

Participants who agree to take part in this study will be asked to complete the following procedures at two time points: before receiving the study intervention (baseline) and 28 days after completing the full vaccine series.

Approximately 200 healthy adults aged 18 years and older from the community will be enrolled in this study. Participants will be randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to one of two study groups: Intervention Group (Vaccine Group): receive the oral cholera vaccine according to the manufacturer's recommended schedule; Control Group (Placebo Group): receive a placebo that looks identical to the vaccine but contains no active ingredient.

The study will measure the following outcomes to evaluate the effects of cholera vaccine:Gut Microbiota Changes, Serum Inflammatory Cytokine Levels and Bowel Habit Changes.
lead_sponsor: Zhejiang Provincial Center for Disease Control and Prevention
primary_outcomes: Change in gut microbiota alpha diversity (Shannon and Chao1 indices), beta diversity (Bray-Curtis dissimilarity), and microbial composition assessed by 16S rRNA gene sequencing of stool samples
Bowel habits
Plasma levels of inflammatory markers, including interleukin-6, interleukin-10, tumor necrosis factor-α, tumor necrosis factor-β, and C-reactive protein
title: Study on Changes in Gut Microbiota, Inflammatory Factors, and Bowel Habits Following Oral Administration of Recombinant B-subunit/Whole Cell Cholera Vaccine in a Community Population

brief_summary:
This study aims to investigate whether a new non-invasive brain stimulation technique, called temporal interference stimulation, can influence brain activity and potentially improve signs of consciousness in patients with severe brain injuries and disorders of consciousness.

After a severe brain injury, some patients may remain unable to communicate or interact normally with their environment because of impaired consciousness. Current treatment options to promote recovery are limited. Temporal interference stimulation is a new technique that uses mild electrical currents applied through electrodes placed on the scalp to target specific areas deep inside the brain without surgery.

In this study, we will use brain imaging data to personalize the stimulation and target a region involved in consciousness regulation, called the thalamus. The effects of the stimulation will be evaluated using brain activity recordings, heart monitoring, and clinical assessments of consciousness and responses to stimulation.

The goal of this research is to determine whether temporal interference stimulation is safe and whether it can produce measurable changes in brain function and behavior in patients with disorders of consciousness. The results may help guide future research on new treatments for recovery after severe brain injury.
primary_outcomes: Coma Recovery Scale - revised (CRS-r)
Simultaneous electroencephalography and electrocardiography recording
title: Temporal Interference Stimulation for Disorders of Consciousness

brief_summary:
Large colorectal polyps removed piece by piece (piecemeal endoscopic mucosal resection) can recur at the resection scar. Detecting this residual or recurrent tissue at surveillance colonoscopy is essential, because it can then be treated endoscopically. Recurrence can be subtle, and the best way to examine the scar has not been established.

This study compares four ways of examining post-polypectomy scars:

high-definition white light endoscopy (WLE) texture and color enhancement imaging (TXI, Olympus) narrow-band imaging (NBI, Olympus) an artificial intelligence computer-aided detection system (GI Genius, Medtronic)

Each scar is examined with all four techniques, in random order. A different expert endoscopist performs each technique, without knowing the findings of the others. Biopsies are then taken from every scar, and any suspicious tissue is removed. Histology is the reference standard.

The main goal is to determine which technique, or combination of techniques, has the highest sensitivity and negative predictive value for detecting recurrence.
lead_sponsor: University Hospital Virgen de las Nieves
primary_outcomes: Sensitivity for histologically confirmed recurrence at the post-polypectomy scar
Negative predictive value for histologically confirmed recurrence
title: White Light, TXI, NBI and Computer-Aided Detection for Recurrence at Post-EMR Scars (PRINCESS)

brief_summary: This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover study will evaluate the acute effects of caffeine consumption on substrate utilization, resting energy metabolism, and mitochondrial function in peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) in healthy young adults. Approximately 10 healthy men and women aged 18 to 35 years will participate. Each participant will complete two experimental visits, receiving caffeine in one visit and placebo in the other, in randomized order. The two visits will be separated by a 48-hour washout period. Participants will attend the laboratory after an overnight fast of approximately 14 hours and will abstain from caffeine, alcohol, and intense physical activity before each visit. Resting gas exchange will be measured before ingestion and 1 and 3 hours after caffeine or placebo administration. Blood samples will be collected at the same time points to isolate PBMCs and obtain plasma for metabolic analyses. Mitochondrial function will be assessed by high-resolution respirometry, and mitochondrial dynamics and morphology will be evaluated using protein analyses and transmission electron microscopy. The study will determine whether acute caffeine consumption alters resting substrate utilization and mitochondrial responses in PBMCs in healthy young adults.
primary_outcomes: Basal mitochondrial respiration in PBMCs

title: Acute Effects of Caffeine on Mitochondrial Function in Peripheral Blood Mononuclear Cells

brief_summary: Oxytocin is a key hormone that regulates uterine contractions during labor. Dural Puncture Epidural Analgesia (DPEA) is a modern technique for labor pain relief that provides faster onset and more reliable analgesia than standard epidural.While it is known that neuraxial analgesia can suppress oxytocin levels, it is unclear whether this effect depends on the stage of labor at which analgesia is administered. This prospective comparative study will enroll 120 pregnant women in spontaneous labor who request DPEA, divided into two groups: Early group (cervical dilation≤5 cm, n=60) and Late group (cervical dilation≥6 cm , n=60). Both groups receive identical DPEA (a total volume of 15 mL containing 0.1% bupivacaine and 100 µg fentanyl is administered through the epidural catheter, following dural puncture with a 26G spinal needle without intrathecal drug injection). The primary outcome is the percentage change in plasma oxytocin from baseline (T-0, before analgesia) to T-Eff (30 minutes after onset of effective analgesia defined as VAS\<2). Patients who received any exogenous oxytocin (induction or augmentation) before T-0 are excluded to ensure that the measured oxytocin represents endogenous production. The study will contribute to understanding how the timing of neuraxial analgesia relative to labor progression affects the endogenous oxytocin system, with potential implications for optimal clinical timing of labor analgesia administration.
primary_outcomes: Percentage change in maternal plasma oxytocin concentration from baseline to T-Eff
title: Effect of Dural Puncture Epidural Analgesia on Oxytocin in Early vs Late Labor

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to evaluate whether an AI-assisted primary care intervention can increase influenza vaccination uptake among patients with chronic diseases and to assess the cost-effectiveness and potential for implementing the intervention in routine primary care.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

1. Does the AI-assisted primary care intervention increase influenza risk perception, influenza vaccine literacy, vaccine confidence, intention to receive influenza vaccination, and influenza vaccination uptake among patients with chronic diseases?
2. Is the AI-assisted primary care intervention cost-effective compared with conventional health education?
3. Is the AI-assisted primary care intervention acceptable, feasible, and potentially sustainable for influenza vaccination promotion?

Researchers will compare patients with chronic diseases who receive the AI-assisted primary care intervention with those who do not receive it to determine whether the intervention improves patients' literacy, confidence, intention, and uptake of influenza vaccination.

Participants will:

1. Be recruited and randomly assigned to the intervention group or control group. Participants in the intervention group will have access to an AI assistant for influenza vaccine-related information and will receive an influenza vaccination recommendation from primary care physicians, while participants in the control group will receive routine health education.
2. Complete a survey questionnaire assessing patients' influenza risk perception, influenza vaccine literacy, vaccine confidence, and intention to receive influenza vaccination.
3. Have their influenza vaccination uptake assessed at the end of the trial.
primary_outcomes: Influenza vaccine uptake
title: Artificial Intelligence-assisted Primary Care for Influenza Vaccination Among Chronic Patients in China (AIPC-Flu)

brief_summary: Individuals who are involved in the criminal-legal system (CLS) are at high risk of drug-related overdose; they also face significant barriers to engaging in substance use disorder (SUD) treatment and recovery support services. To address this public health challenge, this study will test the implementation and outcomes of an evidence-based intervention, Recovery Management Check-ups (RMC), delivered within community-based programs in four Chicago communities that have high rates of drug-related overdose and arrests. The study has the potential to increase uptake of RMC in community-based programs, thereby reducing overdose-related deaths and crime-related costs and improving individual health and community public health.

brief_summary:
The goal of this prospective follow-up study nested within an open-label randomized controlled trial is to investigate the unexpectedly high prevalence of Ascaris lumbricoides infection observed 3-4 months after school-based mass drug administration with ivermectin plus albendazole (IVM-ALB) or albendazole alone (ALB) in Kisoro District, South-Western Uganda. By assessing initial treatment response and subsequent infection dynamics, the study will help clarify whether reduced drug efficacy, suboptimal treatment coverage, reinfection, or a combination of these factors may explain the previous findings.

The main questions the study aims to answer are:

* How effective are IVM-ALB and ALB against A. lumbricoides at 3 weeks, based on egg reduction and cure rates?
* How often do A. lumbricoides and other soil-transmitted helminth infections recur by 3 months?
* How effective are the treatments against Trichuris trichiura and hookworm?
* What can genetic characterization of Ascaris eggs reveal about parasite populations and potential drug resistance markers?

The study will enrol 450 pupils aged 5-14 years from three primary schools, which participated in the previous mass drug administration evaluation. In each school, 150 pupils will be randomly assigned equally to receive a single oral dose of:

* ivermectin (200 µg/kg) plus albendazole (400 mg); or
* albendazole (400 mg) alone.

Each treatment arm will include 225 pupils overall. Children will be included regardless of baseline infection status, following parental/guardian informed consent and child assent. Other pupils will receive routine albendazole under national deworming guidelines.

Stool samples will be collected before treatment and at 3 weeks and 3 months. Duplicate Kato-Katz thick smears will quantify A. lumbricoides, T. trichiura and hookworm eggs. The primary outcome is the arithmetic mean egg reduction rate for A. lumbricoides at 3 weeks. Secondary outcomes include cure rates at 3 weeks, reinfection rates at 3 months, egg reduction and cure rates for T. trichiura and hookworm, and genetic characterization of Ascaris populations and potential resistance markers. Adverse events will be recorded through passive safety monitoring.
primary_outcomes: Egg Reduction Rates (ERRs) for A. lumbricoides infection at 3 weeks post-treatment
title: Follow-up Assessment of Change in Soil-transmitted Helminths Infection Intensity in Uganda

brief_summary: The current classification of acute myeloid leukemias (AML) includes more than 20 different diseases, grouped based on their distinctive genomic characteristics, which reflect substantial heterogeneity. The rationale underlying this project is the idea that an effective diagnostic process and functional dissection of transcriptional heterogeneity at the single-cell level will lead to the identification of cell-intrinsic or cell-extrinsic biomarkers of response to novel therapies in order to improve patient care. In particular, with the study we present here, we intend to obtain data relating to the sub-classification of patients into genomic subgroups with biological and prognostic relevance. Genomic subgroups are categories into which patients affected by the same disease can be divided based on the genetic characteristics found in each patient. The study foresees that part of the biological sample, collected through bone marrow blood sampling, already provided for by clinical practice will be subjected to further analyses. Specifically, DNA and RNA sequencing analyses will be performed on the cells that will be isolated from the bone marrow blood. The objective is to search for molecular markers that may allow better biological and prognostic classification of patients. Molecular markers are particular DNA sequences that, in our study, would enable the classification of patients into subgroups.
interventions: Bulk genotyping of AML samples at diagnosis and relapse, scRNA analysis at diagnosis, scRNAseq and genotyping analysis at day 28 after therapy, spatial transcriptomic analysis at day 0 and 28
lead_sponsor: Fondazione IRCCS Ca' Granda, Ospedale Maggiore Policlinico
primary_outcomes: Definition of a new diagnostic protocol for AML
title: This Study Aims to Improve the Stratification of Patients With Acute Myeloid Leukemia to Enable More Personalized and Effective Treatments, and to Identify and Functionally Validate, at the Single-cell Level, Biomarkers That Can Predict Response to Venetoclax.

brief_summary:
Some patients develop severe heart failure during or after cardiac surgery and require temporary support for circulation and oxygenation. Venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) is a form of life support that circulates blood outside the body through a pump and an oxygenator while the heart recovers.

This retrospective study examines 128 adults who received VA-ECMO for postcardiotomy cardiogenic shock at the National Institute for Cardiovascular Diseases in Bratislava, Slovakia, between January 2013 and June 2026. The study includes 78 patients who started support during the operation or because they could not be separated from cardiopulmonary bypass, and 50 patients who started support later in the intensive care unit after postoperative deterioration.

The main objective is to evaluate the association between the timing of VA-ECMO initiation and death before hospital discharge. Additional outcomes include successful removal of ECMO with survival for at least 24 hours after decannulation, duration of ECMO support, and length of hospitalization. Existing clinical records are used to account for measured differences in patient condition and surgical complexity. All treatment decisions were made by the treating clinical team during routine care.
lead_sponsor: National Institute of Cardiovascular Diseases, Slovakia
primary_outcomes: All-cause in-hospital mortality
title: Timing of VA-ECMO Support During or After Cardiac Surgery

brief_summary: Pain is one of the most common reasons patients seek care in emergency departments. Managing pain effectively is an important part of emergency care because it can improve patients' comfort and overall experience. Wounds that require stitches are also a common reason for visiting the emergency department. Stitching a wound can be painful, both because of the original injury and because of the procedure itself, even when local anesthetic is used. Hypnosis is a state of focused attention in which people may become more responsive to suggestions. It is increasingly used as a non-drug approach to managing pain and anxiety, including during medical and surgical procedures. However, hypnosis is still not widely used in emergency departments, mainly because it usually requires trained staff and additional time. One possible solution is to use a pre-recorded hypnosis audio. Instead of a healthcare professional performing hypnosis directly, the patient could listen to a guided recording during the procedure. Previous research suggests that this approach may provide pain relief similar to that achieved with live hypnosis. HYPNAUS is a study comparing the use of local anesthesia via subcutaneous lidocaine injection with hypnotic guidance via headphones combined with local anesthesia via subcutaneous lidocaine injection alone. We hypothesize that patients receiving hypnotic guidance combined with local anesthesia via subcutaneous lidocaine injection will experience less pain during the stitching procedure.
primary_outcomes: The change in pain level between pain assessed before the stitching procedure and the maximum pain experienced during the procedure.
title: Hypnosis Antalgia Emergency Stitching

brief_summary: This study compared three teaching methods for training resident physicians in lumbar puncture, a critical medical procedure used to collect spinal fluid for diagnosing conditions like meningitis. One hundred thirty-five residents were randomly assigned to either traditional bedside teaching, peer-assisted learning (where trainees practiced in pairs and gave each other feedback), or artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted training using a smart simulator that provided real-time voice feedback on technique. All residents were tested immediately after training and again three months later to see how well they retained their skills. Right after training, all three groups performed equally well. However, after three months, both the peer-learning and AI groups scored significantly higher on practical skills than the traditional group, showing that these newer methods help slow skill decay. The AI group showed the greatest advantages in procedural standardization, pre-procedure assessment, post-procedure care, and operating speed. Meanwhile, residents in the peer-learning group reported the highest satisfaction with classroom interaction and teaching methods. In short, while all three approaches work well for short-term training, AI-assisted and peer-assisted learning are more effective than traditional teaching at helping residents maintain their lumbar puncture skills over time, with AI excelling in technical precision and efficiency, and peer learning offering a more engaging and collaborative learning experience.
lead_sponsor: Second Affiliated Hospital, Zhejiang University, School of Medicine
primary_outcomes: Theoretical knowledge score of lumbar puncture (assessed at T0, T1, and T2)
title: AI-Assisted Instruction Versus Peer Learning for Sustained Lumbar Puncture Competency

brief_summary:
The goal of this cluster-randomized, controlled trial is to learn if a professional development program for childcare educators, called the Boston Healthy Child Care Initiative, can help improve the nutritional quality of meals/snacks served and the availability of physical activity opportunities in childcare programs, and also to learn if this results in improved diet quality and physical activity for young children who attend childcare, especially in under-resourced settings. The main questions it aims to answer are:

Do childcare programs that receive professional development through the Boston Healthy Child Care Initiative improve the nutritional quality of the meals they serve, as measured by the Healthy Eating Index (HEI-2020), and do they also provide more physical activity opportunities to young children throughout the day? Do young children (ages 2-5 years) attending childcare programs that receive the Boston Healthy Child Care Initiative eat more nutritious foods/beverages (as measured by the HEI-2020) and engage in less sedentary time at childcare?

Researchers will compare a group of childcare programs who participate in the Boston Healthy Child Care Initiative, and a sample of children who attend those programs, to a similar group of childcare programs who do not participate to see if the quality of meals served, the amounts of physical activity opportunities scheduled, young children's dietary quality, and the minutes/day spent in physical activity increase from before to after the Boston Healthy Child Care Initiative.

Childcare educator participants will:

* Complete the Boston Healthy Child Care Initiative professional development program (for the intervention group only)
* Share copies of menus, schedules, and written policies about nutrition and physical activity in the childcare program

Child participants will:

* Wear ActiGraph wGT3X-BT accelerometers for two days while at childcare to measure physical activity levels. They will do this for two days each at baseline, midline, and follow-up after the initiative concludes.
* Be observed during mealtimes by trained researchers to visually estimate how much they consume at meals and snacks in childcare.
primary_outcomes: Mean change from baseline to post-intervention in Healthy Eating Index (2020) score for young children's dietary intake while attending childcare.

brief_summary:
Here is the English translation of the summary:

The Clinical Investigation Plan with code CIP-01-25 outlines a single-center, uncontrolled, single-arm clinical study sponsored by Promoitalia Group S.p.A. and conducted at the Casa di Cura Santa Maria La Bruna in Torre del Greco under the responsibility of Principal Investigator Giuseppe Ferraro, with Teia Research S.r.l. acting as the CRO. The primary objective of the study is to evaluate the aesthetic performance and safety of the MD60000 medical device, an intradermal, biodegradable, sterile, and isotonic gel based on 3.3% linear hyaluronic acid integrated with PLA, intended for the correction of skin imperfections caused by physiological skin aging, such as facial wrinkles. The investigation is conducted pursuant to Article 61 of the European Medical Device Regulation 2017/745 (MDR) in order to collect clinical data for regulatory conformity assessment, adhering to ISO 14155 standards and the Declaration of Helsinki.

The study design involves enrolling forty-three adult patients aged between eighteen and sixty-five years with facial skin defects characterized by a baseline score of one or higher on the Lemperle Wrinkle Severity Scale. Patients with skin diseases, active infections, or recent aesthetic treatments in the same anatomical area are excluded, as well as pregnant or breastfeeding women, individuals with a history of allergic reactions to the components, autoimmune diseases, coagulation disorders, or a predisposition to hypertrophic scars or keloids. Participation for each subject ranges between forty-five and sixty-five days, while the overall estimated duration of the entire clinical investigation is approximately six months.

The procedural pathway comprises four main visits. During the first screening and baseline visit, eligibility criteria are verified, informed consent and medical history are collected, and baseline photographic evaluations and wrinkle severity assessments are performed. If conditions permit, the first treatment session can occur on the same day, during which the clinician performs an intradermal injection of MD60000 up to a maximum volume of two milliliters. A similar second treatment session follows after an interval of at least fourteen days. The final phase consists of a follow-up visit thirty days after the second treatment, during which final photographs are taken and data regarding patient satisfaction and safety are collected.

Treatment efficacy is measured using primary and secondary metrics. The primary performance endpoint is defined as the improvement in the Lemperle scale score between the initial baseline visit and the final follow-up, considered clinically relevant if a median reduction of one point or greater is achieved, confirmed statistically using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test. The secondary endpoint assesses the patient's subjective satisfaction using the Global Aesthetic Improvement Scale (GAIS) thirty days after the completion of treatment, met if at least seventy percent of participants report an rating of improved, much improved, or excellent.

Regarding safety, the study evaluates the frequency, severity, and causal relationship of any adverse events or effects occurring during the investigation. The safety profile is considered acceptable in the absence of device-related serious adverse events or device deficiencies, provided that unexpected, mild, device-related adverse events do not exceed a maximum threshold of ten percent. Statistical analysis involves evaluating the Intention-to-Treat (ITT) population set for safety parameters and the Per-Protocol (PP) set for performance metrics.
primary_outcomes: Change from Baseline in Lemperle Wrinkle Assessment Scale (LWSS) Score
Incidence and Severity of Treatment-Emergent Adverse Events (TEAEs) and Device Defect Logs
Investigator Global Aesthetic Improvement Scale (GAIS) Rating
title: Evaluation of the Performance and Safety of the MD60000 Device in the Treatment of Skin Imperfections Due to Aging.

brief_summary:
This study will evaluate whether adding MRG003 to an ongoing treatment regimen can produce confirmed tumor shrinkage in patients with EGFR-positive advanced thyroid cancer whose cancer initially benefited from that regimen and later progressed. The study will also evaluate the safety of the combinations.

Cohort A will include patients with anaplastic or poorly differentiated thyroid carcinoma who previously benefited from lenvatinib plus an anti-PD-1 inhibitor and subsequently progressed. They will continue lenvatinib and the same anti-PD-1 inhibitor, with MRG003 added.

Cohort B will include patients with radioactive iodine-refractory differentiated thyroid carcinoma who previously benefited from lenvatinib and subsequently progressed. They will continue lenvatinib, with MRG003 added.

MRG003 will be given intravenously at 2.0 mg/kg every 3 weeks. The study plans to enroll 39 participants: 24 in Cohort A and 15 in Cohort B. The first 3 participants in each cohort will undergo an initial 6-week safety assessment before further enrollment is allowed. If additional safety assessment is needed, up to 6 participants who can be evaluated for dose-limiting toxicity will be assessed within the planned cohort enrollment. The main outcome is the proportion of patients in each cohort whose tumors shrink or disappear within 12 weeks after MRG003 starts, with the response confirmed at least 4 weeks later and by Week 18. Scans obtained before MRG003 is added provide the new baseline. Disease control is assessed at Week 12. Other response and survival outcomes are followed for up to 12 months after MRG003 starts. Safety follow-up continues during study treatment and for 90 days after the last study treatment dose, with longer follow-up of unresolved events as needed.
lead_sponsor: Sun Yat-Sen Memorial Hospital of Sun Yat-Sen University
primary_outcomes: Early Confirmed Objective Response Rate Within 12 Weeks After Addition of MRG003
title: MRG003 Added to Ongoing Treatment After Progression in EGFR-Positive Advanced Thyroid Cancer

Aim: Evaluate whether combined rutin + ascorbic acid supplementation reduces the incidence of vancomycin-induced nephrotoxicity (VAN) in adult patients, compared to ascorbic acid alone and a control group.

Design: Prospective, open-label, randomized controlled, three-arm clinical trial; 120 adult patients recruited from Internal Medicine departments at Ain Shams University Hospital.

Population: Adults (≥18) receiving vancomycin for ≥7 days for MRSA infections, without prior kidney injury, proteinuria/hematuria, or other antioxidant/nephrotoxic drug use.

brief_summary:
This randomized controlled trial aims to evaluate the effects of the Benson relaxation exercise and the Jacobson relaxation exercise-administered to individuals undergoing urinary tract stone surgery-on pain, vital signs (blood pressure, pulse, respiratory rate, oxygen saturation, and body temperature), and anxiety levels. Postoperative pain and anxiety are common issues that can negatively affect vital signs. Non-pharmacological interventions, such as relaxation exercises, may help reduce these adverse effects.

Participants will be randomly assigned to one of three groups: the Benson relaxation exercise group, the Jacobson relaxation exercise group, or the control group receiving routine postoperative care. Relaxation exercises will be performed two times a day for 15 minutes each, provided the individual's general condition is stable. Outcomes such as pain, anxiety, and vital signs will be measured at baseline (pre-test), on postoperative day 0, and on postoperative day 1 after each session. The findings of this study are expected to provide evidence regarding the effectiveness of relaxation exercises as supportive nursing interventions in the postoperative care of patients undergoing urinary tract stone surgery.

brief_summary:
Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains one of the deadliest malignancies, with 5-year survival around 12% despite advances in surgery, chemotherapy, and radiotherapy. Existing ablative therapies (RFA, microwave, irreversible electroporation) are limited by thermal injury risk, proximity to vessels/ducts. Novel local therapies that can be integrated with systemic regimens are urgently needed. Histotripsy is a non-thermal focused ultrasound modality that uses controlled cavitation to mechanically liquefy tissue without thermal coagulation or ionizing radiation, with precision under real-time ultrasound guidance. Preclinical and early translational work in pancreatic models shows that histotripsy can safely ablate pancreatic tissue while sparing major vessels and ducts in large-animal models, and can alter the tumour microenvironment (TME) with increased release of damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs), enhanced dendritic cell and macrophage activation, and increased CD8+ T-cell infiltration in murine pancreatic tumours.

This proposal aims to evaluate the safety, local tumour control, and immunologic effects of histotripsy in pancreatic cancer especially PDAC, positioning it as a platform to enhance responsiveness to contemporary systemic therapies.

The HistoSonics Histotripsy System is now registered in the Medical Device Administration Control System from Department of Health in Hong Kong (HKMD no: 252842).

brief_summary:
This is an exploratory, prospective, single-center, open-label, 1:1 randomized controlled study. The study compares two surgical methods for benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH): ultrasound-guided prostate suspension and conventional prostate suspension. BPH is a common condition in older men that can cause lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS), such as frequent urination, weak urine stream, and difficulty emptying the bladder. The purpose of this study is to learn whether using ultrasound guidance during prostate suspension can improve urinary symptoms and urine flow more than the standard procedure, while preserving sexual function and maintaining safety.

About 20 men aged 50-80 years with BPH and bothersome LUTS will be enrolled. Eligible participants must have an IPSS score of 12 or higher, a maximum urine flow rate (Qmax) of 15 mL/s or less, a prostate volume of 30-100 mL, and a post-void residual urine (PVR) of 250 mL or less. They must be dissatisfied with medication or refuse long-term medication and be able to give informed consent. Men with prior prostate surgery, suspected or confirmed prostate cancer, neurogenic bladder, urethral stricture, bladder neck contracture, bladder stones, recurrent urinary tract infection, active urinary infection, bleeding disorders, acute urinary retention, or current participation in another interventional trial cannot take part.

Participants will be randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to the experimental group or the control group. The experimental group will receive ultrasound-guided prostate suspension. In this procedure, the standard UroLift prostate suspension is performed with ultrasound guidance, and at least one additional suspension implant is placed on each side. The control group will receive the standard NeoTract UroLift System procedure. Both procedures are minimally invasive and are performed through the urethra without cutting prostate tissue. The study is open-label, meaning participants and surgeons know which procedure is used, but the staff who assess outcomes will be blinded to group assignment to reduce bias.

The main outcome is the change in IPSS at 12 months after surgery. Secondary outcomes include changes in Qmax, quality of life (IPSS-QoL), PVR, sexual function (IIEF-5), complications, and retreatment rate. Follow-up visits will occur at about 1, 3, 6, and 12 months after surgery. The total study duration is about 36 months.

All surgery has risks. Possible risks include bleeding, infection, pain, urinary symptoms, urinary retention, implant-related problems, or the need for further treatment. The study team will monitor participants closely and provide standard medical care as needed. This study may help doctors understand whether ultrasound-guided prostate suspension offers better symptom relief than the standard procedure. Participation is voluntary, and participants may withdraw at any time without affecting their usual medical care.
primary_outcomes: Change in International Prostate Symptom Score (IPSS) from Baseline to 12 Months After Surgery
title: Ultrasound-Guided vs. Conventional Prostate Suspension in BPH: An Exploratory Study

The PD-1 monoclonal antibody serplulimab combined with chemotherapy has shown potential in improving response rate and survival for advanced gastric cancer. Regulation of tumor metabolism and immune microenvironment may further enhance the efficacy of immunotherapy. Ferrous sulfate supplementation improves anemia and immune cell metabolism; succinate, as a key metabolic signaling molecule, participates in inflammation and immune regulation. This study intends to explore the synergistic effect and safety of oral ferrous sulfate/ferrous succinate in serplulimab plus SOX neoadjuvant therapy.

brief_summary:
The purpose of this clinical investigation is to evaluate the clinical performance, safety, and clinical benefit of the BrainProtect System in reducing early postoperative neurological complications in adult participants undergoing elective coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) with cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB).

The investigation aims to verify the claim that real-time detection and correction of cerebral autoregulation (CA) impairment during CPB improves neurological outcomes compared to standard perioperative management. The study is designed to demonstrate superiority of BrainProtect-guided management over standard care.

This is a Multicenter, two-arm, blinded, randomized controlled pivotal (confirmatory) clinical investigation of a non-CE marked investigational medical device. Adult participants undergoing elective coronary artery bypass graft (CABG) surgery requiring cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) will be randomized in a 1:1 ratio to either the investigational group or the control group.

In the investigational group, standard perioperative management during CABG with CPB will be performed. Real-time cerebral autoregulation (CA) monitoring using the BrainProtect System will be applied during CPB.

In the control group, standard perioperative management during CABG with CPB will be performed. Conventional systemic hemodynamic monitoring will be used. The BrainProtect System will not be used, and no real-time cerebral autoregulation monitoring data will be available to the clinical team.

Postoperative neurological outcomes (POCD and POD) will be assessed in both groups using predefined standardized neuropsychological tests and CAM-ICU assessments during the early postoperative period. In addition, the length of the index hospitalisation and occurrence of hospital readmission within 31 days after surgery and the reason for readmission will be recorded.
primary_outcomes: Number of Participants With Postoperative Delirium and/or Postoperative Cognitive Dysfunction (Composite Neurological Outcome)
title: BrainProtect-guided, Real-time Cerebral Autoregulation Monitoring and Protection of Brain During Cardiac Surgery With Cardiopulmonary Bypass Requiring Heart-lung Machine

The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if an electronic version of the Psychometric Hepatic Encephalopathy Score (PHES) works as well as the standard paper version to diagnose minimal hepatic encephalopathy (MHE) in adults with liver cirrhosis. The main questions it aims to answer are:

Do the total scores of the electronic and paper tests match for the same patient? Do both tests classify patients as having MHE or not in the same way? Researchers will compare the electronic PHES to the paper PHES to see if they produce equivalent results.

Participants will:

Complete two cognitive tests (one paper-based and one electronic) on two separate days.

Provide information about their medical history and complete routine blood tests as part of their standard care.

brief_summary:
PURPOSE:

To investigate the effects of low-load resistance training combined with blood flow restriction on muscle strength, functional performance, and cancer-related fatigue in colorectal cancer survivors with probable sarcopenia.

Although low-load resistance training with blood flow restriction shows promise, CRC-specific randomized evidence remains limited (Patterson et al., 2019; Arnold et al., 2017).

HYPOTHESES:

It is hypothesized that low-load blood flow restriction resistance training will lead to significant improvements in muscle strength and functional performance, and a significant reduction in cancer-related fatigue in colorectal cancer survivors with probable sarcopenia.

RESEARCH QUESTION:

Does low-load blood flow restriction resistance training will lead to significant improvements in muscle strength and functional performance, and a significant reduction in cancer-related fatigue in colorectal cancer survivors with probable sarcopenia?
