brief_summary:
The number of adults and children living with obesity is increasing worldwide. Once childhood obesity has developed, more than 80% of children carry the obesity into adulthood, with a high risk of cardiometabolic disease, poor mental health, and decreased life expectancy. Parental obesity is a strong predictor of intergenerational obesity and is closely associated with a child's body composition from childhood through to adulthood.

Obesity pharmacotherapy effectively reduces body weight. In adults, we have shown that combining obesity pharmacotherapy with supervised exercise improves weight-loss maintenance compared with pharmacotherapy alone. Emerging evidence suggest that exercise may also limit weight regain after treatment cessation. Together with evidence linking physical activity, sleep, and eating behaviours to weight regulation, these findings support combining pharmacological treatment with interventions targeting multiple modifiable behaviours. Personalised, data-driven feedback may further facilitate sustained behavioural change, but few interventions have integrated these approaches within the family setting.

This 58-week randomized clinical trial aims to investigate the separate and combined effects of a data-driven, multimodal family-based intervention and semaglutide treatment for parents with obesity on body fat percentage and other health-related outcomes in parents and children.

Approximately 400 families will be randomly assigned to one of four groups combining data-driven, multimodal family-based intervention or standard health advice with semaglutide or placebo. The data-driven, multimodal family-based intervention focuses on physical activity, diet, sleep and mental well-being.

The trial will include families with at least one parent with obesity and at least one child aged 5 to 12 years with overweight or obesity. Participating parents with obesity will receive semaglutide or placebo once weekly for 28 weeks.

The main outcomes are changes in body fat percentage in participating parents and children. Other outcomes include changes in body mass index (BMI) in parents and age- and sex-adjusted BMI, known as BMI z-score, in children. Families will participate in the main trial for 58 weeks and complete an additional follow-up assessment at week 104 after randomization.
primary_outcomes: Change in body fat percentage
title: FutureShape Family

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether transarterial embolization (TAE) can relieve pain and improve well-being in adults with inflammatory arthritis that remains active in only one large joint (wrist, elbow, shoulder, ankle, knee or hip) despite anti-inflammatory drugs, joint injections and physiotherapy. The researchers expect that more people treated with TAE than with a sham (simulated) procedure will reach low pain and a good overall assessment of their health one month after the procedure.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does TAE increase the proportion of participants who reach low pain and a good overall assessment of their health one month after the procedure, compared with a sham procedure?
* Is TAE safe, and does it improve quality of life and reduce the need for medication over three months?

TAE is a minimally invasive procedure. A thin catheter is guided through an artery in the groin or wrist to the small vessels that feed the inflamed lining of the joint, and tiny resorbable gelatin particles are injected to temporarily reduce the abnormal blood flow that sustains inflammation and pain. Researchers will compare TAE with a sham procedure to find out whether any benefit comes from the embolization itself rather than from the experience of undergoing a procedure.

Participants will:

* Be randomly assigned (like flipping a coin) to TAE or to the sham procedure. Neither the participants nor the doctor who evaluates them will know which procedure they received.
* Undergo the procedure in the angiography room with light sedation. The sham procedure takes place in the same room, with the same team, sedation and duration, but without any puncture of the artery, contrast medium or X-rays.
* Attend visits before the procedure and 1 week, 1 month and 3 months after it, answer questionnaires on pain and quality of life, and keep a diary of symptoms and medicines for 7 days after the procedure.

After 3 months, participants who received the sham procedure will be offered TAE.
interventions: Transarterial embolization with resorbable gelatin microspheres
primary_outcomes: Proportion of participants with pain VAS ≤15 mm and Patient Global Assessment ≤20 mm.
title: Transarterial Embolization Versus Sham Procedure in Adults With Treatment-Resistant Inflammatory Arthritis of a Single Large Joint

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether low-intensity focused ultrasound (LIFU), a non-invasive form of brain stimulation, can change brain activity and improve thinking and decision-making in adults with obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD). The main questions it aims to answer are:

Can active LIFU change activity in brain pathways involved in OCD? Can active LIFU improve the ability to control thoughts and actions?

Researchers will compare active LIFU with sham LIFU to see whether active LIFU causes changes in brain activity and performance on behavioral tasks.

Participants will:

Complete questionnaires and behavioral tasks. Have magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scans to measure brain activity and identify the area to receive LIFU.

Receive both active and sham LIFU on separate visits. Have MRI scans and complete behavioral tasks after each LIFU session. Complete assessments of OCD symptoms, safety, and possible side effects.
primary_outcomes: Changes in functional connectivity between the ALIC and prefrontal cortex
Change in reaction time on the Multi-Source Interference Task (MSIT)
Change in accuracy on the Multi-Source Interference Task (MSIT)
title: Low-intensity Ultrasound for Individuals With Obsessive-compulsive Disorder

brief_summary:
This study will test and refine a type of brain training called functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) neurofeedback in healthy adults. Neurofeedback allows participants to view real-time information about their own brain activity while undergoing an MRI scan and to attempt to modify this activity using mental strategies.

The study focuses on a brain circuit involving regions important for decision-making, attention, and emotion. Participants will complete two neurofeedback MRI sessions. In one session, feedback will be based on activity within individual brain regions. In the other session, feedback will be based on communication (functional connectivity) between brain regions, guided by prior knowledge of their anatomical connections. The order of the two sessions will be randomized.

The main objective is to determine whether incorporating information about the anatomical organization of brain circuits can improve fMRI neurofeedback. The findings will be used to optimize neurofeedback methods for future studies, including studies involving psychiatric disorders such as obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD).
lead_sponsor: The University of Texas Health Science Center, Houston
primary_outcomes: Neurofeedback Modulation Performance as assessed by the mean change in the neural target signal
title: Neuroanatomically Informed fMRI Neurofeedback in Healthy Adults

brief_summary: This dual-design study-encompassing a cross-sectional descriptive phase and a controlled clinical trial-aims to investigate the prevalence and associated risk factors of Molar Incisor Hypomineralization (MIH), while evaluating the therapeutic efficacy of resin infiltration (ICON) for treating mild MIH lesions in permanent incisors among school children aged 7 to 11 years across selected primary schools in Northern Vietnam. The primary research questions seek to delineate the current epidemiological profile of MIH alongside its pre-, peri-, and postnatal biological determinants, while assessing the longitudinal clinical outcomes of resin infiltration (ICON) regarding color change ΔE, lesion depth penetration, and aesthetic restoration compared to control groups. In the interventional phase, outcomes of the resin infiltration cohort will be evaluated against control protocols (such as topical fluoride varnish application or observation/untreated controls) to quantify improvements in color stability, remineralization, and defect dimensions. Participating pediatric subjects will undergo comprehensive oral examinations to index MIH severity on first permanent molars and incisors, alongside standardized questionnaire-based interviews with guardians to record medical history. Children presenting with mild incisor defects enrolled in the clinical trial will receive treatment with resin infiltration or comparative controls, followed by standardized digital photography and spectrophotometric color assessment (using the VITA Easyshade V device), with structured post-operative follow-up evaluations scheduled at baseline 1 month, 2nd month, 3rd month, 6th month, and 12th month to measure long-term treatment longevity and outcomes.
primary_outcomes: Color Improvement and Lesion Masking Effect
title: Molar-Incisor Hypomineralization and Resin Infiltration

brief_summary:
Given the impact that hot flashes and night sweats can have on daily life during the menopausal transition, our team has developed a therapist-guided online cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT)- based program to help individuals manage these symptoms. An online program may help address systemic barriers to in-person care, such as cost, time, travel, and caregiving needs.

The broad aim of this pilot clinical trial is to examine the experience of a four-week therapist-guided online CBT-based program for menopause-related hot flashes and night sweats. The primary objective of this study is to evaluate the acceptability and feasibility of the four-week online program, including how participants experience the program and how well they are able to complete it at home. The secondary objective is to explore whether the program may help with hot flashes and night sweats, and related concerns such as sleep, mood, anxiety, and quality of life. Exploratory analyses will examine whether changes in these outcomes are maintained three months after completing the program.

Researchers will compare participants who receive the program immediately with participants who wait four weeks before receiving it.

Participants will:

* Complete online questionnaires about their symptoms and well-being.
* Complete four weekly online lessons and activities.
* Meet briefly with a guide each week for guidance and support.
* Complete follow-up questionnaires after the program and three months later.

brief_summary:
Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is a major global health burden, affecting approximately 589 million adults worldwide in 2024, with the number projected to reach 853 million by 2050 .Despite advances in glucose-lowering therapy, a substantial proportion of patients remain inadequately controlled despite multiple medications .

Hypercortisolism is a potentially reversible contributor to poor glycemic control. Excess cortisol promotes hepatic gluconeogenesis, impairs peripheral insulin sensitivity, and adversely affects β-cell function, thereby contributing to insulin resistance and hyperglycemia .Clinical manifestations of Cushing syndrome may overlap with common features of T2DM and obesity, making mild or clinically unapparent hypercortisolism difficult to recognize .

Recent evidence has highlighted the relevance of hypercortisolism in patients with difficult-to-control T2DM. In the multicenter CATALYST study, 23.8% of 1,057 participants with inadequately controlled T2DM had an abnormal 1-mg dexamethasone suppression test (DST), defined as post-DST cortisol \>1.8 µg/dL (50 nmol/L) . However, data regarding the prevalence and clinical characteristics of hypercortisolism among Egyptian patients with difficult-to-control T2DM are lacking.

The Endocrine Society recommends biochemical testing for suspected Cushing syndrome using validated first-line tests, including the 1-mg overnight DST, late-night salivary cortisol, or urinary free cortisol .Therefore, determining the prevalence and characteristics of hypercortisolism in difficult-to-control T2DM may help identify a potentially treatable contributor to persistent hyperglycemia and provide locally relevant evidence for clinical practice.
primary_outcomes: Prevalence of hypercortisolism in patients with difficult-to-control type 2 diabetes mellitus
title: Prevalence and Predictors of Hypercorticolism in Patients With Difficult to Control Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus

brief_summary: Bipolar disorder (BD) is often diagnosed 5 to 10 years after first symptoms, worsening prognosis. "Bipolar At-Risk" (BAR) criteria have been developed to identify people who may be in an early, prodromal stage of BD, but their long-term clinical course is not well characterized. BAROMETRE is a prospective, multicenter, naturalistic study following two groups of hospitalized psychiatric patients aged 18-65 for 36 months: patients meeting BAR criteria (without prior manic/hypomanic episode) and patients with an already diagnosed bipolar disorder (type 1 or 2), used as a clinical reference group. No experimental treatment is imposed; patients receive usual care. At inclusion, 1, 12, 24 and 36 months, participants undergo structured psychiatric interviews and clinician-rated scales (YMRS, MADRS, CGI, C-SSRS, Sachs Bipolarity Index); at 6, 18 and 30 months they complete self-report questionnaires by phone or online (BDI, HCL-32, PSQI, WHOQOL). The main hypothesis is that a clinically significant proportion (around 20%) of BAR patients will convert to a full bipolar disorder (first DSM-5 manic/hypomanic episode) within 36 months. Secondary aims are to describe and compare mood, functioning, quality of life, suicidality, sleep, substance use, trauma/PTSD symptoms, and care pathways (hospitalizations, treatment changes) between the two groups, and, exploratorily, between BAR patients who convert and those who do not. This pilot study aims to better characterize the evolution of at-risk states and generate hypotheses for larger confirmatory studies.
interventions: Structured clinical follow-up and psychometric assessment
Structured clinical follow-up and psychometric assessment

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if Zhixuan Analgesic Tablet works to treat frequent episodic tension-type headache in adults aged 18-60 years. It will also learn about the safety of Zhixuan Analgesic Tablet.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does Zhixuan Analgesic Tablet reduce the number of headache days compared with placebo within each 4-week interval during the 12-week treatment period?
* What medical problems do participants have when taking Zhixuan Analgesic Tablet? Researchers will compare Zhixuan Analgesic Tablet (4 tablets per dose, 3 times per day) to a matching placebo (a look-alike tablet that contains no active drug) to see if Zhixuan Analgesic Tablet reduces overall headache burden - including headache days, the amount of acute analgesic medication needed, the duration and severity of headaches, and the impact of headache on daily life.

Participants will:

* Take Zhixuan Analgesic Tablet or a matching placebo 3 times per day for 12 weeks
* Keep a headache diary to record headache days, headache duration and severity, and any acute analgesic medication used
* Attend scheduled clinic visits for check-ups and safety monitoring
* Complete the Headache Impact Test (HIT-6) and a global self-assessment of treatment effectiveness at the end of the treatment period
primary_outcomes: monthly headache days
title: Treatment of Tension-type Headache by Zhixuan Analgesic Tablets

Its prevalence varies considerably according to the population studied and the diagnostic criteria applied. A recent global systematic review and meta-analysis estimated the prevalence of PCOS among adult women to be approximately 12.1% according to the Rotterdam criteria, compared with 7.9% using the National Institutes of Health (NIH) criteria and 12.7% using the Androgen Excess-PCOS Society criteria.

brief_summary: This randomized controlled study compared three educational approaches for teaching fall-risk assessment to first-year nursing students. The study included 81 nursing students who were randomly assigned in equal numbers to a podcast group, a video group, or a face-to-face instruction group. All three groups received the same educational content on the importance of fall prevention, fall risk factors, systematic fall-risk assessment, and use of the ITAKI Fall Risk Scale, but the content was delivered using different instructional methods. Students' theoretical knowledge of fall-risk assessment was measured before and immediately after the educational intervention. One week later, students' clinical fall-risk assessment performance was evaluated during clinical practice while they assessed patients under their care. The study aimed to compare students' theoretical knowledge and clinical assessment performance across the three instructional approaches.
primary_outcomes: Theoretical Knowledge of Fall-Risk Assessment
title: Podcast and Video Learning for Fall-Risk Assessment in Nursing Students

Participants followed an individually prescribed Mediterranean-style energy-restricted diet and attended weekly follow-up visits throughout the intervention. Body weight and body composition were assessed at weekly follow-up visits, while perceived stress and biochemical parameters, including serum cortisol, were evaluated at baseline and at the end of the 12-week intervention. Sleep quality and physical activity were also assessed at baseline. The study further examined whether perceived stress, serum cortisol, sleep quality, and physical activity were associated with the magnitude of body weight and fat mass loss achieved during the dietary intervention.
primary_outcomes: Change in Serum Cortisol Level

brief_summary:
The goal of this study is to evaluate the anti-wrinkle, firming, moisturizing and repairing efficacy of a test facial cream after single use and 12 weeks of continuous use via clinical evaluation, instrumental measurement, image analysis and participant self-assessment.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

Does the test cream produce immediate anti-wrinkle, firming, moisturizing and repairing effects on facial skin after single use? Can 12-week continuous use of the test cream sustainably improve facial skin condition in terms of wrinkles, laxity, hydration and skin repair? This is a single-center clinical study with a self-controlled before-and-after design. Around 70 healthy Chinese women aged 25-50 will be randomly divided into an instrumental group and a questionnaire group, with no fewer than 40 valid clinical test samples and 60 valid questionnaire samples. The study uses four products, including one test cream and three auxiliary skincare products.

Participants will:

Use the test cream once on-site and continuously at home for 12 weeks with matched auxiliary products.

Attend six scheduled visits at key time points: 2 weeks before product use for washout and screening (T-2W), baseline detection and immediate assessment after single product use (T0+Timm), 1 week after continuous product use (T1W), 4 weeks after continuous product use (T4W), 8 weeks after continuous product use (T8W), and 12 weeks after continuous product use (T12W) .

Complete group-specific assessments: the instrumental group will undergo instrumental tests, clinical evaluation and image collection; the questionnaire group will finish clinical screening and self-assessment.

Receive skin indicator detection and efficacy evaluation at all designated time points to verify the product's skincare effects.
interventions: Test facial cream (topical skin care product)

brief_summary:

The main questions the study aims to answer are:

* Does topically applied menthol (gel and roll-on formats) reduce pain when applied in the Recovery Zone immediately after a marathon?
* What are the sensory attributes (e.g., cooling sensation) of topically applied menthol (gel and roll-on) when used in the Recovery Zone immediately after a marathon?
* How do participants assess the effects of topically applied menthol products used during and/or after a marathon on pain relief, performance, recovery, and sleep-related quality-of-life outcomes? Researchers will evaluate participant-reported pre- and post-application pain scores in the Recovery Zone immediately following the marathon and post-race outcomes to assess analgesic effectiveness, sensory attributes, and quality-of-life outcomes associated with Biofreeze use.

Participants will:

* Provide documented informed consent prior to participation.
* Self-select to use Biofreeze products during and/or after the race.
* Complete one or both of the following:

  1. End of Race Questionnaire (includes pain score before and after Biofreeze application, sensory assessments, and demographics).
  2. Post-Race Questionnaire (includes retrospective recall of pain relief, product use, sensory experience, sleep-related outcomes and demographic data).

brief_summary:
Videolaryngoscopy generally improves the glottic view compared with direct laryngoscopy, yet a good view does not always translate into easy delivery of the tracheal tube. Existing classifications describe either the laryngeal view (Cormack-Lehane grade, percentage of glottic opening) or the overall difficulty of intubation (Intubation Difficulty Scale), but none characterizes which specific mechanism produces difficulty during videolaryngoscopic intubation.

This observational study evaluates a component-based score developed to describe procedural difficulty encountered during videolaryngoscopic tracheal intubation.

The score comprises four components, each graded 0 to 2 (total range 0 to 8):

view-tube concordance, restricted epiglottic movement, need for additional laryngoscopic manoeuvres, and need for tube-shaping adjustment.

Adult patients undergoing elective surgery under general anaesthesia with tracheal intubation performed using a Macintosh-blade videolaryngoscope were assessed. The primary objective is to examine the association between the total score and procedural outcomes: intubation time, number of attempts, and first-attempt success. Secondary objectives include the relationship of the score with the Intubation Difficulty Scale, the Video Classification of Intubation, percentage of glottic opening, preoperative airway assessment parameters and operator experience.
primary_outcomes: Association between the total score and intubation time
Association between the total score and the number of intubation attempts
Association between the total score and first-attempt intubation success
title: A Novel Score for Procedural Difficulty During Videolaryngoscopic Intubation

brief_summary:
This study investigates whether a resistance training program can help patients recovering from hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) for hematologic malignancies.

HSCT is a vital treatment, but it comes with a high risk of severe complications. These include opportunistic infections caused by low white blood cell counts (neutropenia) and acute graft-versus-host disease (aGVHD), where donor cells attack the patient's body. Additionally, more than half of patients suffered from severe cancer-related fatigue during or after transplantation, which significantly lowers their quality of life. Currently, treatments for these complications rely almost entirely on medication.

The purpose of this study is to see if an 8-week elastic band resistance training program can speed up blood cell recovery, reduce the severity of aGVHD, shorten hospital stays, and alleviate cancer-related fatigue.

A total of 86 patients preparing for HSCT at Taipei Veterans General Hospital will be randomly assigned to one of two groups:

1. The Resistance Training Group (43 patients): Participants will perform 45-minute elastic band exercises three times a week, starting four weeks before their transplant and continuing until four weeks after.
2. The Control Group (43 patients): Participants will receive standard routine care.

The study will compare the two groups by measuring how many days it takes for white blood cells to recover, the occurrence and severity of aGVHD, muscle strength (hand grip and lower limbs), fatigue levels, and the total length of hospital stays.
primary_outcomes: Score on the Brief Fatigue Inventory - Taiwan Version (BFI-T) for Cancer-Related Fatigue
title: Effects of Resistance Training on Recovery During Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation

brief_summary:
Claudin 18.2 (CLDN18.2) is a molecular target expressed in a subset of gastric and gastroesophageal junction (GEJ) adenocarcinomas. Zolbetuximab, a chimeric monoclonal antibody targeting CLDN18.2, has shown clinical benefit in combination with chemotherapy for CLDN18.2-positive unresectable advanced or recurrent gastric cancer, and in Japan, FLOT plus durvalumab is expected to become a standard perioperative treatment for locally advanced gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma. This trial evaluates whether adding zolbetuximab to FLOT plus durvalumab further improves the pathological response of neoadjuvant chemotherapy in CLDN18.2-positive, locally advanced, resectable gastric or GEJ adenocarcinoma.

This is a single-arm, open-label, multicenter, investigator-initiated phase II trial conducted at four sites in Japan. Eligible participants are adults (18 years or older) with previously untreated (no prior chemotherapy, radiotherapy, or immunotherapy), histologically confirmed gastric or GEJ adenocarcinoma classified as cT2-4 and/or cN+, M0 by the UICC/TNM Classification (8th edition), confirmed to be CLDN18.2-positive (moderate or greater membranous staining in 75% or more of tumor cells) by immunohistochemistry, with an ECOG performance status of 0 or 1.

The primary endpoint is the histological complete response rate (Grade 3) on the surgical specimen, assessed by a central pathological review committee. Key secondary endpoints include the incidence of adverse events, the treatment completion rate through surgery, the dose intensity of neoadjuvant chemotherapy, the R0 resection rate, and the histological response rate (Grade 2 or higher).
primary_outcomes: Histological complete response rate (Grade 3), per central pathological review
title: Zolbetuximab, Durvalumab, and FLOT Combination Neoadjuvant Chemotherapy for CLDN18.2-Positive Gastric Cancer or Gastroesophageal Junction Adenocarcinoma

brief_summary: This study is aiming at exploring the association between periodontitis and dry eye disease, which are both chronic inflammatory diseases that might have common pathogenic mechanisms. It is a cross-sectional study being conducted on four specific groups: a healthy group, periodontitis only, dry eye disease only, and a group with both periodontitis and dry eye disease. For all individuals, both clinical periodontal and ophthalmic parameters and assessments are being recorded. The study also includes collection of both saliva and tear samples from all individuals for later analysis of inflammatory biomarkers. Saliva samples will be collected using the drooling method, while tear samples will be collected using Schirmer strips. The levels of specific inflammatory biomarkers, including interleukin-6 (IL-6), matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs), and tissue inhibitors of metalloproteinases (TIMPs), will be investigated using ELISA. The study aims to investigate the association between periodontal and ocular surface inflammation as well as investigate the common inflammatory pathways for both periodontitis and dry eye disease. These investigations might contribute to a better understanding of the systemic correlation that links both periodontal and ocular health.
primary_outcomes: Probing pocket depth

brief_summary: This retrospective observational study aims to assess the real-world effectiveness of conservative treatment (bracing and specific exercises) in patients with idiopathic scoliosis treated with an Evidence-Based Personalised Approach (EBPA). Clinical records of about 30,000 patients collected in the institutional database of ISICO (Italian Scientific Spine Institute, Milan, Italy) since 2003 will be analysed. For each patient, the expected natural history (risk of progression without treatment) will be estimated with two validated prognostic models, IS-GROWTH and BrAIST-Calc. The outcome observed at skeletal maturity will be compared with the predicted risk to measure treatment effectiveness in preventing the 30°, 45° and 50° Cobb thresholds. Secondary aims include subgroup analyses by age at onset (infantile, juvenile, adolescent), validation of the prognostic models in the Italian population, over- and under-treatment rates, drop-outs and compliance, quality of life of patients and parents, and comparison between treatment tools.
primary_outcomes: Proportion of patients exceeding clinical severity thresholds (30°, 45° and 50° Cobb) at skeletal maturity, compared with predicted natural history

brief_summary:
Before surgery, patients are asked to fast so the stomach is empty and stomach contents cannot enter the lungs during anesthesia. Long fasting is uncomfortable and can raise blood sugar and stress responses in older adults. Giving a carbohydrate drink up to 2 hours before surgery is part of enhanced recovery (ERAS) programs. It is not clear whether a maltodextrin drink or sugar water leaves less fluid in the stomach of older patients.

This randomized, double-blind study enrolls patients aged 60 years and older who are having elective lower limb orthopedic surgery under spinal or epidural anesthesia at Prof. Ngoerah General Hospital in Denpasar, Indonesia. Participants are assigned by chance to drink 400 mL of either a maltodextrin carbohydrate drink or sugar water 2 hours before anesthesia. The amount of fluid in the stomach is measured with bedside ultrasound before the drink and 2 hours after it. Blood glucose is measured before the drink, 2 hours after it and 6 hours after surgery. The neutrophil-lymphocyte ratio, a blood marker of inflammatory stress, is compared before surgery and 6 hours after surgery.

The results are intended to show which drink is better suited to older surgical patients and to support safer and more comfortable fasting practice.
primary_outcomes: Gastric volume 2 hours after carbohydrate loading
title: Maltodextrin Versus Sugar Water Carbohydrate Loading and Gastric Volume in Geriatric Lower Limb Orthopedic Surgery

Bladder cancer patients often face frequent clinic visits for BCG treatment, creating time, cost, and require help from caregivers or family members. brief_summary:
The goal of this study is to evaluate whether a voice-activated call light system enables people in a rehabilitation facility who have limited use of their arms and hands to call for help more independently and reliably than with their previous call light access method. The study will also examine client confidence, family confidence and peace of mind, staff confidence, staff effort, system reliability, and the level of disruption to routine care. The main questions to be answered are:

1. People with what etiologies benefit most from access to the voice-activated call light system?
2. How reliable is the voice-activated call light system in alerting staff to a client's need for assistance?
3. How confident are clients, family members, and staff in the reliability of the voice-activated system for alerting staff of a client's need for assistance?
4. How does access to the voice-activated call light system compare to traditional call light systems regarding staff effort and disruption to routine care? Participants with limited upper extremity movement will use the voice-activated call light system as needed during normal daily activities for up to 90 days. At study initiation, clients with limited upper extremity movement, staff members working with those clients, and family members of the clients will complete a brief questionnaire about their experiences using the existing call light system. At approximately Days 30, 60, and 90, they will complete brief questionnaires about use of the voice-activated call light system and its effectiveness.

Change in client-, staff-, and family-reported confidence in client's ability to activate a call light system reliably.

Reliability of voice-activated call light system use by people with limited upper extremity movement.
Willingness of participants with limited upper extremity movement, staff members, and family members to continue using a voice-activated call light device after termination of the study.
title: Evaluation of a Voice-Activated Call Light System for Clients With Limited Upper-Extremity Mobility

brief_summary: There is emerging evidence that the order in which food is consumed in a meal, known as the "nutrient sequence", can have protective health effects against obesity and metabolic disease. These studies show that consuming food sources rich in protein before consuming carbohydrates will significantly lower blood glucose levels equivalent to many glucose-lowering medications. This nutrition intervention can have tremendous therapeutic potential in individuals who are pre-diabetic and prevent the onset of obesity. Surprisingly, however, there are no studies to date that have comprehensively tested this efficacy in young health adults. This research proposal will define the response of nutrient sequencing in young healthy individuals to determine if this intervention can improve metabolic profiles such as normalizing blood glucose levels to healthy parameters in order to prevent obesity and type 2 diabetes. We will 1) test if the metabolic benefits of Nutrient Sequencing can extend across different populations in NY state, and 2) define the mechanism of the metabolic response to nutrient sequencing interventions by capturing participant circulating blood proteome and metabolome.
primary_outcomes: Blood Glucose
title: The Effect of Nutrient Sequencing in Healthy Adults

brief_summary:
This clinical study aims to compare the effects of time-restricted eating and a personalized energy-restricted diet on anthropometric measurements, body composition, biochemical parameters, blood pressure, handgrip strength, menopausal symptoms, and sleep quality in obese postmenopausal women. The study is a 12-week, open-label, controlled, parallel-group clinical trial with a quasi-randomized allocation design. The coordinating center is the Department of Internal Medicine, Faculty of Medicine, Gazi University, and the study will be conducted at the Internal Medicine Outpatient Clinic of Cihanbeyli State Hospital in Konya, Türkiye.

A total of 40 postmenopausal women are planned to participate, with 20 participants in each group. Participants will undergo an initial medical examination and baseline assessments, including demographic and health information, dietary habits, menopausal symptoms, sleep quality, physical activity, and dietary intake. Anthropometric measurements, body composition, handgrip strength, blood pressure, and biochemical parameters will also be assessed.

Participants in the intervention group will follow a time-restricted eating schedule in which they will consume food within an 8-hour daily eating window and fast for 16 hours. The eating window will begin between 8:00 AM and 12:00 PM and will be determined by the participant. During the fasting period, water, unsweetened tea, plain coffee, and plain mineral water will be permitted. Participants in the control group will follow a personalized energy-restricted diet providing approximately 25% less energy than their estimated energy requirements. The diet will be planned according to menopausal nutrition recommendations and individual preferences.

Dietary intake will be monitored every 2 weeks. Anthropometric measurements, blood pressure, and handgrip strength will be assessed every 4 weeks. All baseline assessments will be repeated after the 12-week intervention period. The study hypothesis is that time-restricted eating will result in greater improvements than the personalized energy-restricted diet in anthropometric measurements and body composition, biochemical parameters, blood pressure, handgrip strength, menopausal symptoms, and sleep quality in obese postmenopausal women.
primary_outcomes: Change in body weight
Change in menopausal symptoms
Change in sleep quality
title: Time-Restricted Eating and Personalized Energy-Restricted Diet in Obese Postmenopausal Women

brief_summary:
Despite complete (R0) resection, patients with EGFR-mutant stage IIA-IIIB non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) still face a substantial risk of postoperative recurrence. Although adjuvant EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors have improved disease-free survival, conventional fixed-duration adjuvant therapy is applied uniformly to all patients and does not distinguish those who genuinely require treatment from those who could be safely spared. Circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) profiling enables minimal residual disease (MRD) detection that is both earlier and more accurate than imaging, and has therefore emerged as a promising tool for individualizing postoperative adjuvant therapy.

This prospective, real-world, interventional study will enroll 50 patients with resected (R0), EGFR 19del or L858R mutant, stage IIA-IIIB non-squamous NSCLC. For three years after surgery, adjuvant treatment is dynamically guided by serial MRD testing performed 3-10 days and 4 weeks (±7 days) after surgery and every 3-6 months thereafter. Patients with a positive MRD result at either of the first two time points receive aumolertinib-based adjuvant therapy, with the regimen determined by the mutations detected in blood: aumolertinib monotherapy (110 mg once daily) when only the EGFR mutation is detected, or aumolertinib combined with chemotherapy (pemetrexed plus carboplatin for four cycles, followed by pemetrexed maintenance) when co-mutations are detected. Patients whose MRD remains negative undergo observation with regular ctDNA monitoring; if MRD turns positive or imaging progression occurs, aumolertinib-based adjuvant therapy is initiated according to the same rules. Treatment is discontinued once MRD becomes undetectable; patients with persistently negative MRD over three years receive no aumolertinib. After three years, subsequent treatment is at the investigator's discretion.

The primary endpoint is the 2-year disease-free survival (DFS) rate, defined as the proportion of patients remaining free from recurrence or death for at least 24 months after surgery. Secondary endpoints include the 2-, 3-, and 5-year overall survival rates, 3-year total treatment cost, incremental cost-effectiveness ratio, rate of timely postoperative recurrence diagnosis, and cumulative duration of aumolertinib treatment; exploratory analyses will assess the association between ctDNA/MRD molecular features and clinical efficacy. This study aims to establish a dynamic MRD-guided precision adjuvant strategy that avoids overtreatment while improving outcomes in resected EGFR-mutant NSCLC.
primary_outcomes: 2-year disease-free survival (DFS) rate
title: MRD-Guided Aumolertinib-Based Adjuvant Therapy for Resected EGFR-Mutant NSCLC

brief_summary:
This study is evaluating the safety and effectiveness of virus-specific cytotoxic T lymphocytes (vCTLs) for treating difficult-to-control viral infections caused by cytomegalovirus (CMV), adenovirus (ADV), Epstein-Barr virus (EBV), or BK virus in children, adolescents, and young adults with weakened immune systems. Eligible participants include recipients of hematopoietic stem cell transplantation, solid organ transplantation, and patients with primary immunodeficiency disorders.

vCTLs are immune cells collected from a related donor and selected to recognize and fight specific viruses. The cells are manufactured using the CliniMACS® Cytokine Capture System and administered by intravenous infusion. Additional infusions may be given if viral infection persists.

The study will assess the safety of vCTL therapy, including the risk of graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) and infusion-related reactions, as well as its ability to reduce viral infection, improve clinical outcomes, and support survival. Participants will be monitored for approximately 12 weeks after their final vCTL infusion. Participants will all receive vCTLs; there is no comparison group.

Participants will:

1. Have donor-derived vCTLs manufactured for infusion using the CliniMACS Cytokine Capture System
2. Receive the vCTLs through an intravenous infusion
3. Be monitored for side effects and infusion reactions, viral levels through blood testing, clinical outcomes, including response to treatment, survival, and time without detectable virus
primary_outcomes: Occurrence of Grade 3 or higher acute graft-versus-host disease (GVHD)
Occurrence of Grade 3 or higher infusion-related reactions
title: 25BT056: Basket Study of Viral Cytotoxic T Lymphocytes

Phase 1 will identify the recommended dose through dose escalation, followed by a randomized comparison of two candidate dosing regimens (dose optimization). In Phase 2, the selected dose will be tested in independent cohorts by tumor type.

brief_summary:
This is an investigator-initiated, randomized, open-label, parallel-controlled clinical study designed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of locally administered Tris-CAR-T cells in adults with newly diagnosed glioblastoma.

A total of 60 postoperative participants with IDH-wildtype WHO CNS grade 4 glioblastoma will be randomized 1:1 to the experimental group or the control group, with 30 participants in each group.

Participants in the experimental group will receive Ommaya reservoir implantation followed by local intratumoral or intraventricular Tris-CAR-T cell injections, and then standard temozolomide-based chemoradiotherapy and adjuvant temozolomide. If tumor progression occurs during Tris-CAR-T cell therapy, Tris-CAR-T treatment will be discontinued, and participants will transition to standard temozolomide-based chemoradiotherapy.

Participants in the control group will receive standard temozolomide-based chemoradiotherapy and adjuvant temozolomide.

The primary objective is to evaluate progression-free survival. Secondary objectives include overall survival, 12-month objective response rate, 12-month disease control rate, and safety.
primary_outcomes: Progression-Free Survival (PFS)
title: Tris-CAR-T Cell Therapy Targeting CD44 and CD133 in Newly Diagnosed Glioblastoma

brief_summary:
HYROX© is a fast-growing fitness competition that combines long-distance running with functional exercises such as sled pushes, rowing, and weightlifting movements. Although the sport has attracted more than a million participants worldwide, little scientific research has looked at the health, body composition, and physical fitness of the people who compete in it.

This study will compare body composition, fitness, and performance between two groups of HYROX© participants: those competing at a recreational (amateur) level and those competing at an elite level.

Adult volunteers (ages 18-65) who train for or compete in HYROX© will be invited to take part. Researchers will measure body composition using a whole-body scan (DXA), skinfold thickness, and muscle ultrasound; resting metabolism; daily physical activity (using a wearable activity tracker); muscle strength and jumping ability; aerobic fitness (a treadmill running test); and short-burst power (a cycling test). Participants will also complete questionnaires about their motivation to exercise, their diet, and their use of dietary supplements, and will wear a heart rate monitor and activity tracker during an official HYROX© competition.

The results will help researchers, coaches, and athletes better understand how the bodies and training needs of HYROX© athletes differ by competitive level, which may support the development of safer and more effective training programs.
primary_outcomes: Maximal Oxygen Uptake (VO2peak)
title: Physiological and Performance Characteristics of HYROX Athletes

brief_summary: The study objective is to determine the real-world safety and effectiveness of LV009 therapy for 3 potential indications: (1) refractory or relapsed hematologic cancers (acute lymphoblastic Leukemia, B cell Lymphomas, multiple myeloma), (2) auto-immune diseases, (3) de-sensitization of patients awaiting organ transplant or AAV-based gene therapy who have pre-existing anti-HLA or anti-AAV antibodies. This is an observational study designed to determine the real-world safety and effectiveness of LV009, an in vivo CAR-T therapy, among patients with hematologic cancers, auto-immune diseases, or HLA/AAV sensitization. Following the administration of LV009, patient will be monitored for toxicity and response to treatment. No subjects will be withdrawn from the study, and subjects could freely drop out from the study anytime, simply by not showing up. The study objective is to determine the real-world safety and effectiveness of LV009 therapy for 3 potential indications: (1) refractory or relapsed hematologic cancers (acute lymphoblastic Leukemia, B cell Lymphomas, multiple myeloma), (2) auto-immune diseases, (3) de-sensitization of patients awaiting organ transplant or AAV-based gene therapy who have pre-existing anti-HLA or anti-AAV antibodies.
primary_outcomes: Incidence and Severity of Post-Treatment Adverse Events
title: Real-world Clinical Effectiveness & Safety LV009, an in Vivo CAR-T for the Treatment of Hematologic Cancers, Auto-immune Diseases & HLA/ AAV Sensitization.

brief_summary:
The goal of this randomized clinical trial is to evaluate whether the use of a vertical birthing chair during the active second stage of labor improves fetal head descent and rotation. The effects will be assessed objectively by intrapartum ultrasonography, and effects on labor progress and maternal and neonatal outcomes. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does the use of a vertical birthing chair improve intrapartum ultrasonographic parameters of fetal head descent and rotation compared with the standard semi-recumbent position?
* Does the use of a vertical birthing chair affect the duration of the second stage of labor, mode of delivery, perineal injury, postpartum blood loss, maternal childbirth experience, and neonatal outcomes?

Researchers will compare women assigned to use a vertical birthing chair with women assigned to the standard semi-recumbent position to determine the effects of maternal position during the active second stage of labor.

Participants will:

* Be randomly assigned to either the vertical birthing chair group or the standard semi-recumbent position group during the active second stage of labor.
* Undergo intrapartum ultrasonographic assessment of fetal head descent and rotation.
* Be evaluated for the duration and mode of delivery, episiotomy and perineal trauma, postpartum blood loss, and neonatal outcomes.
* Complete the Childbirth Experience Questionnaire (CEQ) to assess their childbirth experience.
interventions: Using a vertical birthing chair during the active second stage of labor
primary_outcomes: 1. Change in Angle of Progression From Baseline to 30 Minutes
title: Effect of a Vertical Birthing Chair on Labor

A total of 200 participants will be included in four groups of 50 participants each. Periodontal clinical measurements, including plaque index, gingival index, bleeding on probing, probing depth, and clinical attachment level, will be recorded. Venous blood samples will be collected for DNA isolation and analysis of MTHFR gene polymorphisms. The study will investigate whether MTHFR gene polymorphisms are associated with periodontal clinical parameters and hypertension.

brief_summary:
During surgery, telephone calls, conversations, equipment problems and other events may distract the operating team. Some events interrupt the progress of the operation. The surgeon's workload and anxiety, together with how well the team works together, may also be related to events that occur during surgery.

ORCHESTRA is an observational study of patients undergoing colorectal or anal surgery in a single hospital. Trained observers record distractions during routine operations. After each operation, the surgeon reports workload and anxiety, and an observer assesses teamwork. Intraoperative adverse events are graded using a standard severity classification. The study examines how these measurements are related. It does not assign treatments, introduce distractions or change routine surgical care.
interventions: Naturally occurring operating-room distractions and human factors
lead_sponsor: National and Kapodistrian University of Athens
primary_outcomes: Intraoperative adverse-event severity assessed by ClassIntra
title: Operating-Room Distractions, Surgeon Workload, Anxiety, Teamwork and Intraoperative Adverse Events (ORCHESTRA)

brief_summary: This is a prospective, single-arm, multicenter, phase II clinical study designed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of iparomlimab and tuvonralimab (QL1706) combined with cetuximab and mFOLFIRI as first-line treatment for recurrent or metastatic colorectal cancer. A total of 55 participants with low-level microsatellite instability (MSI-L) or microsatellite stable (MSS)/mismatch repair-proficient (pMMR) and RAS/BRAF wild-type tumors will be enrolled. Enrolled participants will receive iparomlimab and tuvonralimab (5 mg/kg, Q3W, Day 1) + cetuximab (500 mg/m², Q2W, Day 1) + irinotecan (180 mg/m², Q2W, Day 1) + leucovorin (LV) (400 mg/m², Q2W, Day 1) + 5-FU (400 mg/m², Q2W, Day 1). After 12 cycles of the chemotherapy phase, participants who achieve CR, PR, or SD will then receive maintenance therapy with iparomlimab and tuvonralimab (5 mg/kg, Q3W, Day 1) + cetuximab (500 mg/m², Q2W, Day 1) + leucovorin (LV) (400 mg/m², Q2W, Day 1) + 5-fluorouracil (5-FU) (400 mg/m², Q2W, Day 1) until disease progression, intolerable toxicity, investigator determination that the participant is no longer benefiting, withdrawal of informed consent, completion of 2 years of iparomlimab and tuvonralimab treatment, or other protocol-specified reasons.
interventions: QL1706 combined with cetuximab and mFOLFIRI
lead_sponsor: The First Affiliated Hospital with Nanjing Medical University
primary_outcomes: Progression-Free Survival (PFS)
title: A Prospective, Single-Arm, Multicenter, Phase II Clinical Study of Iparomlimab and Tuvonralimab (QL1706) Combined With Cetuximab and mFOLFIRI Regimen as First-Line Treatment for Recurrent or Metastatic Colorectal Cancer

brief_summary:
This is a multicenter, prospective, observational cohort study of patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), individuals with pre-COPD, and healthy participants. The study will enroll approximately 400 participants, including individuals with pre-COPD, patients with stable COPD at different GOLD stages, patients with acute exacerbation of COPD, and healthy controls.

Participants will not be assigned to any study intervention. Clinical information, pulmonary function, imaging information, traditional Chinese medicine syndrome assessment, and biological samples will be collected according to the study protocol. Multi-omics analyses, including metagenomics, metabolomics, transcriptomics, and proteomics, will be used to characterize molecular features associated with COPD stages and traditional Chinese medicine syndromes. Participants will be followed to evaluate clinical characteristics, exacerbations, pulmonary function changes, and multi-omics features over time.

brief_summary: This randomized, double-blind, controlled clinical trial evaluates the effectiveness and safety of combined mesenchymal stem cell (MSC) secretome and repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) for motor recovery in patients with subacute ischemic stroke. Participants will be randomized to either an intervention group receiving intravenous MSC secretome combined with high-frequency ipsilesional rTMS or a control group receiving placebo infusion and sham rTMS. The intervention is administered once weekly for 8 weeks. The primary outcome is change in motor function measured using the Fugl-Meyer Motor Scale. Secondary outcomes include changes in quantitative electroencephalography biomarkers, including sensorimotor rhythm, delta-theta-to-alpha-beta ratio, and beta coherence, as well as spasticity assessed using the Modified Ashworth Scale and treatment-related adverse events.
primary_outcomes: Change in Fugl-Meyer Motor Scale Score

brief_summary:
This randomized controlled trial will investigate whether delaying the start of morning training from 7:00 AM to 9:00 AM improves nocturnal sleep and change-of-direction performance in elite badminton athletes. A total of 38 athletes with an established morning-training routine will be randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to either a usual morning-training group starting at 7:00 AM or a delayed morning-training group starting at 9:00 AM. Both groups will follow the same training content, duration, intensity, coaching arrangements, and recovery procedures for three weeks.

Nocturnal sleep will be objectively monitored using wrist-worn activity monitors, with total sleep time as the primary outcome. Change-of-direction performance will be assessed using the modified 505 test. Additional outcomes will include sleep opportunity, sleep efficiency, sleep onset latency, nighttime awakenings, bedtime and wake time, nap duration, 24-hour total sleep, training load, and training adherence.

The study aims to determine whether a later morning-training schedule can provide athletes with greater sleep opportunity without compromising training quality or physical performance.

brief_summary: This pilot study is testing a new treatment for people who still have frequent headaches months after a mild traumatic brain injury, with about half of the participants coming from military or veteran backgrounds. The treatment, called "Mindful RAVANS," pairs a guided breathing meditation with gentle electrical stimulation delivered through a small clip in the left ear, timed so the stimulation pulses each time the person breathes out. The idea is that stimulating the vagus nerve, which helps calm the body's stress response, while practicing mindfulness may ease headaches, stress, and other lingering concussion symptoms. Participants are randomly assigned so that three out of four get the real treatment and one out of four gets a look-alike "fake" version, and everyone attends four 30-minute sessions over two weeks, followed by online surveys at two, four, and eight weeks. Because it's an early-stage study, the main goal isn't to prove the treatment works but to find out whether people can stick with it, find it comfortable, and like it enough to justify a larger trial.

A web-based verification workflow is developed, and CPU-based runtime performance is evaluated to explore its clinical potential.

brief_summary: Tracheostomy is a surgical procedure that involves creating an opening in the trachea and bringing it to the skin surface to form a stoma. It may be performed as an emergency or elective operation. The main indications include relief of upper airway obstruction, protection of the lower respiratory tract, and facilitation of assisted ventilation in critically ill patients. Further studies are needed to identify the patient populations that may benefit from early tracheostomy. Therefore, this study was conducted to evaluate early tracheostomy (≤7 days) compared with late tracheostomy (\>7 days) in relation to the occurrence of ventilator-associated pneumonia, duration of mechanical ventilation, length of hospital stay, and 30-day mortality in critically ill patients with traumatic head injury.
primary_outcomes: Ventilator-Associated Pneumonia
title: Outcomes of Early Versus Late Tracheostomy in Critically Ill Patients Due to Head Injury: A Randomized Controlled Trial
